h2: Visual testing in Denver: aviation checks, high-altitude weathering and the rules that apply
html:
Visual testing in Denver: aviation checks, high-altitude weathering and the rules that apply

Visual testing (VT) is the NDT method of looking at a surface under controlled conditions, directly or with optical aids, and recording what is found against stated acceptance criteria. Around Denver it is the first examination on aircraft, pipelines, plant equipment and structures across the Front Range. Atlantis trains VT technicians online to SNT-TC-1A and sends VT inspectors from Houston for Colorado site work.

What makes visual inspection an NDT method. A casual look is not VT. Under ASME Section V Article 9, direct visual examination needs the eye within about 24 inches (600 mm) of the surface at an angle of at least 30 degrees, with at least 100 footcandles (1,000 lux) of light at the surface. Remote visual examination with borescopes, video probes or crawler cameras must resolve detail at least as well as direct viewing would. The procedure, the technician's certification and the light-meter check belong in the record, which is what separates NDT VT from a walk-around.

Aviation at Denver International. Southwest Airlines opened a 130,000-square-foot Technical Operations hangar at Denver International Airport on March 24, 2022. It holds three Boeing 737s inside, with room for eight more outside, supports scheduled overnight maintenance for what was then a fleet of nearly 730 Boeing 737s, and is home to more than 100 Denver-based technical operations employees. Overnight checks like these are largely visual work against task cards, with borescope inspection extending it inside engines, and the method and acceptance limits come from the manufacturer's maintenance data.

Weathering a mile above sea level. Denver's altitude, strong sunlight, wide daily temperature swings and freeze-thaw cycles show up first as visual findings: chalking and cracking of coatings on the sunny side of tanks and piping, failed sealant and jacketing seams that let water into insulation, ice damage at low points and drains, and frost heave around foundations and pipe supports. Recording those findings with consistent locations lets the next survey tell new damage from old.

Who sets the rules in Colorado. Colorado's boiler program is run by the Division of Oil and Public Safety in the Department of Labor and Employment. Colorado is not an OSHA State Plan state, so federal OSHA, including the process safety management standard for covered process units, applies to most private-sector sites. Pipeline VT at excavations follows the operator's procedure under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195.

  • Direct and remote visual examination to ASME Section V Article 9
  • External surveys of piping and vessels that mark corrosion under insulation and support damage
  • Weld visual acceptance to AWS D1.1 or the referencing construction code
  • Borescope examination of boiler drums, headers and closed piping

The method is explained on the visual testing page, and scopes that combine VT with UT or other methods start from NDT inspection services or CUI inspection. Technicians can take VT training, practice on the Practical NDT visual testing simulator, and see local enrollment on the Denver NDT training page. For site work, send the asset list and access details through the Denver VT request.
